findings.title: Pipeline settings policy and its config keys are wired in two places
findings.description:
`one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` and `open_pipeline_session` (`src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:455-461`) each repeat the same sequence. Each reads `pipeline.user_settings`, feeds it to `pipeline_setting_sources`, and reads `pipeline.auto_memory`. The key strings `"pipeline.user_settings"` and `"pipeline.auto_memory"` are literals at both sites and again in `keys.py`. That conflicts with the project rule "define once, reference everywhere". A rename or a new policy input would have to be changed in both places, and the two could drift. The two sites also resolve the config cwd differently: `cwd or "."` in one and `Path.cwd()` in the other.

Add one helper next to `sdk_settings_options` in `providers/sdk/settings.py`, for example `pipeline_settings(cwd)`. It would own the key names and the policy resolution, and both callers would use it.

findings.title: Test fakes return `object`, forcing 35 type suppressions in one test file
findings.description: `scripted_session`, `sdk_text`, `sdk_result` and `typed_config` are all annotated `-> object`. As a result, `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py` carries 35 `# type: ignore` or `pyright: ignore` comments (`session.dispatch`, `ledger.active`, and others). The Python rules require strict pyright on tests, because test bugs can mask code bugs. Suppressing at every call site defeats that. Annotate `scripted_session` as `SDKExecutionSession`, `_ledger_after` as `BackgroundLedger`, and the message builders with the SDK message types. Related: `test_failed_reconnect_marks_session_unusable` uses `pytest.raises(Exception, match="E2BIG")`, which is broader than needed. `ProviderError` or `CLIConnectionError` would be tighter.

findings.title: Auto-memory is now always disabled for non-pipeline SDK agents, including `sq serve`
findings.description: Previously `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY` was set only when `setting_sources == []`. Now `kwargs["env"]` is always set, and `AgentConfig.auto_memory` defaults to `False`. Any caller that doesn't opt in, `sq serve` agents included, now runs with auto-memory off. This matches the stated D11 policy of an explicit per-path choice, so it is not a defect. It is a user-visible behavior change for `sq serve`, and it should be called out in the release notes. The `setting_sources=None` path still reaches the CLI with its default of loading user settings. That is documented as `SETTING_SOURCES_CLI_DEFAULT` and is not a new risk.

findings.title: Type suppressions at the settings boundary
findings.description: `SdkSettings.setting_sources` is `list[str]`, but `ClaudeAgentOptions` expects its `SettingSource` literal list. This forces `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]` here and `# type: ignore[arg-type]` on `base_env=` in `provider.py:86`. Typing the `SdkSettings` field with the SDK's literal type, or building the options in one place (see the first finding), would remove both. `SDKExecutionSession.auto_memory` also infers its value from env-variable presence rather than storing it. That is correct today, but it couples the property to the env encoding.

findings.title: Preset-ness is derived in two places
findings.description: `_PRESET_MODES` re-encodes which `SystemPromptMode` values mean "preset" in the persistence layer. The knowledge belongs on the enum, for example an `uses_preset` property, next to `describe_system_prompt`. Separately, the constant sits between `_NOT_COMPUTED` and `_NOT_OFFERED`, which splits that pair. The `describe_system_prompt` docstring refers to "the table above", which is a comment inside `AgentConfig`. That reference is fragile if the class is edited.

findings.title: Exception handling and failure observability in the new SDK session code
findings.description: `_stop_background` catches a broad `Exception`, with `noqa: BLE001` and a comment explaining that the SDK raises a bare `Exception`. It logs with `logger.exception` and continues to the next task id. `_reconnect` records `unusable_reason`, logs at ERROR and re-raises. `_require_usable` then fails every later call. The idle-timeout stop, the discarded follow-up turn and the stream-ended-with-agents-running cases all emit WARNING or raise `ProviderError`, and tests assert the logged signal for each. This satisfies the failure-mode enumeration rule.

findings.title: Bool config coercion and the settings-policy test matrix
findings.description: Bool parsing is lenient (case and whitespace), and an invalid value raises a `ValueError` that names the key. The CLI maps that error to exit code 1. `test_path_settings_policy` drives each automated SDK path's real builder, for reviews, PR review, pipeline session, one-shot dispatch, summary, audit and PR composer. It asserts that no path resolves to `None` setting sources. That covers the main regression risk of this change.
